summary:
Fix round 5 of M2 is done. Rule A is now exact for every pair of round parts, and verify is green (603 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped).

Rule A: a Cylinder inside a Cylinder now uses the farthest point of its cap circles from the hider's axis. This is V1's search, with two changes I checked against a 50-digit truth:
- The offset across the axis is now taken by its parts. V1's version, on the whole offset, erred by up to 1.5e-11; this one stays within 5e-16.
- The near-parallel cutoff is 1e-8 instead of 1e-6. At 1e-6 the error was 1.8e-13 just under the cutoff; at 1e-12 it was 7e-11.

The search runs only where two cheap bounds leave a cap undecided, and it is charged UNITS_PER_RIM = 28 (measured: 1.19 µs a cap against 43 ns a unit). The bounds are a new upper bound, sqrt(|m|² + 2r|p| + r²), and the circle's point toward p as the lower bound. The lead's root-mean-square lower bound is valid but sits up to 0.67 below the truth, so it would leave far more caps undecided.

On the three sets the bounds decide every Cylinder-in-Cylinder test (151,712 of them), so the search never runs there. No decision differs from the always-searched rule or from the old bound. On V1's rods and pucks, 6,235 of 35,352 tests are searched and none differs. Every truly hidden rod and puck is now cleaned. V1's pucks sword is back to the truth's row (Sharpening 0.1302 Normal, was 0.3739 Hard).

Bit-compare, final tree against the tree before, on 33,389 plausible + 1,340 corpus + 193 fixture designs: nothing moves (no verdict, measure, mass, probe or unit), so no units needed re-pinning.

Text (SPEC §4.4, §4.9, §14.11, §16.18, §17.1 O9, §17.2, E-S2.12, Cover's header):
- O9 (b) now states the real price. A thin plate lying flat anywhere on a round guard's side reads 0 while it truly shows 37.3 % at a side's middle and 38.9 % at a corner, up to about 48 % for a CornerWedge.
- O9's ways to narrow it now include a finer prism (64 sides cost P2 2.9× the units, 128 sides 8.4×; 5 and 6 of the 10 worst valid designs then pass the cap) and reading the side's cut by the face's plane. The latter I tried in a copy only, not in the build: it reads all 81 plates within 0.25 points of the truth and moves no verdict on the three sets.
- The Ball circle's price now quotes the verifiers' climbs, reproduced (2.40 % at r 0.3, 9.63 % at r 3).
- Checkpoint gaps over 0.35 ms come from garbage collection. With a forced collection at each checkpoint, no run of the 85 designs exceeds 0.26 ms. The text now says T-PERF-01 asserts the gap limit on the F, C and X fixtures and reports P1–P5 and the worst designs against it.

All minors are applied: V1's AXIS_TIE text and three tests, and V2's script and comment fixes. Two new tests fail on the tree before as they should; 12 mutants (V1's three and nine of the new rule A) are all killed. CoverBrute now reads the cap rims its own way (dense sampling with a bound), which brackets the decision. VerdictPrecision passes on all six seeds.

Nothing is committed and Studio was not touched.

deviations: Two changes to V1's rimFarthest. (1) The centre's offset is taken across the axis by its parts (K = |m|² + r²) instead of on the whole offset, which erred by up to 1.5e-11. (2) The parallel cutoff is 1e-8 instead of 1e-6, which left 1.8e-13 just under it. Both were measured against a 50-digit truth.

Lower bound: instead of the suggested RMS (valid but up to 0.67 low), I use the circle's point toward p, an actual point of the circle. The upper bound is sqrt(|m|² + 2r|p| + r²), tighter than the old |m| + r. These two agree for parallel axes and for a tangent puck, so V1's pucks and tangent rods need no search.

UNITS_PER_RIM is 28 (the measured cost), not the 45 V1 floated. It charges each open cap searched, never order-dependent. The rule-A loop now reports at each round hider; this does not fire on any set.
'List them in that folder's README': I added the fix5 rows to cover/README.md, as rounds 1–4 did, rather than a README inside fix5/.

I prototyped the strip (side's cut by the face's plane) in a scratch copy to check the lead's reasoning. The claim that a near-tangent face just inside lies within any circumscribed polygon of its cut does not hold for faces parallel to the axis: their cut is an exact strip, and the trial reads all 81 plates near their truth. O9 states this; for oblique faces the ellipse/polygon caveat stands. No build change.

Item 4: model building is charged only about 0.4 of its time (97–116 ns a unit against about 43). I did not raise UNITS_PER_FACET: that would move every design's units and the cap's boundary (the cluster's 24 Ball models are 29,184 units), and the gaps past 0.35 ms are collections in any case.
V2's report quotes a Block 0.0635 × 0.0341 × 0.0925 (2.3957 %), but its logs keep no literals for it. I reproduced the highest logged parts instead: 2.3965 % at r 0.3 and 9.6347 % at r 3.
openIssues: O9 (b) on a Cylinder is still open for the designer: thin plates lying anywhere on a round guard's side read 0 while truly showing up to about 48 %. The strip trial fixes faces parallel to the axis cheaply, moves no verdict on the sets and lowers units. If it is adopted, CoverBrute must read the strip too, and oblique faces would still need an ellipse polygon.

Models are charged about 0.4 of their time (97–116 ns a unit). This is harmless for the cap (24 models at most), but it makes model stretches the longest checkpoint gaps once collections are excluded. M3 or S8 could rebalance UNITS_PER_FACET with a BALANCE_VERSION bump.

Checkpoint gaps past 0.35 ms remain possible on single runs (up to 0.74 ms on the cluster) because of collections. §17.2 keeps fewer allocations, or an incremental GC step at each checkpoint, as the remedy for S8 and S2.
rodtilt still keeps 2 rods that poke out of their Cylinder by more than EPS_GEOM (3.385 % and 2.200 %). That is O9 (a), unchanged.
No Studio timing was taken. The finer prism's units were measured only on P2, F3, C09, the cluster and the worst designs.
